newsitem.title: USA: Mass. treasurer announces gubernatorial run.
newsitem.headline: Mass. treasurer announces gubernatorial run.

text.p: Massachusetts Treasurer Joseph Malone announced Wednesday he was entering the race for the 1998 Republican nomination for state governor.
Speaking in front of an old textile mill in his hometown of Waltham, Malone pledged to fight for a cut in the state income tax to 5 percent from 5.9 percent.
"It's time for government to keep its promise, it's time to lower the rate back to five percent," he said.
President Clinton's nomination Wednesday of Massachusetts Gov. William Weld as ambassador to Mexico opened the door to other contenders to the office.
"I want to announce early because it's clear with the Weld situation there's a bit of vacuum. I want to let people know that I want that job," Malone said.

However, North Carolina Sen. Jesse Helms, chairman of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee that must first consider ambassadorial nominations, is in a position to block Weld's confirmation and has vowed to do so.
Weld, a Republican, has hinted in recent months that he may run for a third term as governor if he is not appointed to another position. But Malone doubted that Weld would run again.

"I think the odds of that happening are just about one percent of one percent. If it happens, I would certainly yield to the governor and wish him well and do everything I can to get him elected to a third term," he said.
If Weld stays out of the race, Malone's main rival for the Republican nomination is expected to be Lt.Gov. Paul Cellucci.

Democratic Congressman Joseph Kennedy, son of slain former U.S. Attorney General Robert Kennedy, is expected to seek the Democratic nomination for governor. Massachusetts Attorney General Scott Harshbarger has said he will also seek the Democratic nomination.
